name: Izhar
overview: Izhar was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Ashhur and Helah. His mention is brief and limited to his parentage, with no additional notes or distinguishing attributes recorded. He is referenced in the genealogical records of 1 Chronicles 4:7.
namesAndTitles: The name Izhar appears as a proper name in Scripture without a recorded meaning or divine origin. Its biblical significance is limited to its identification of this individual in the genealogical context.
familyAndRelationships: Izhar is explicitly described as the son of Ashhur and Helah, establishing his immediate family lineage. Beyond this, Scripture does not record further family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Izhar's significance lies in his inclusion in the genealogical listings of the tribe of Judah, highlighting the continuity of God's covenant people through successive generations. Though not prominent in narrative events, his mention affirms the detailed preservation of Israelite lineage, which ultimately points to the fulfillment of God's promises through Christ.
